name: Review Assigner
description:
Picks code reviewers from CODEOWNERS and keeps one card per pull request up to date in your review room. In each CODEOWNERS team the PR touches, it picks the person with the fewest open reviews.

How to use

  • /review 1234, /review repo#123 or a PR URL: picks the reviewers and posts the card.
  • /review 1234 @user: names the reviewers yourself. No draw.
  • /review workload: shows who has open reviews, on which PRs, and for how long. Only you see the answer.
  • On the card, Take it asks which teams you will review for: yours come preselected, and you can pick any team on the card. Leave it empty to join as an extra reviewer. Reassign swaps or removes a reviewer, or draws again.
  • The card follows GitHub: approved, changes requested, commented, then merged or closed.

Setup

  • GitHub token: read-only, with read:org to list team members (and repo read access for private repositories). If the app cannot read a team, /review says which one.
  • Review room and Repositories (one owner/repo per line, the first is the default).
  • Rocket.Chat and GitHub users: one rocketchat-username github-login pair per line. Linked people are mentioned on cards; others show as their GitHub login.
  • How reviewers are picked: Balanced (default: fewest open reviews first, then whoever covers more teams, then not recently picked) or Random.
  • Out of office: GitHub logins to leave out of draws, optionally with until YYYY-MM-DD.
  • One reviewer can cover several teams: on by default, so someone in several of the PR's teams covers them all. Turn it off to give each team its own reviewer.
  • Webhook (optional): add a GitHub webhook to https://<workspace>/api/apps/public/79a6aec5-9fcd-4c1f-8892-8a74ada7656b/github?token=<Webhook secret>, content type JSON, events Pull requests and Pull request reviews, then turn on GitHub webhook is set up. Without it, the app checks GitHub every 5 minutes.
